We can view probabilistic PCA as defining a thin pancake-shaped region of high probability—a Gaussian distribution that is very narrow along some axes, just as a pancake is very flat along its vertical axis, but is elongated along other axes, just as a pancake is wide along its horizontal axes. This is illustrated in figure 13.3. PCA can be interpreted as aligning this pancake with a linear manifold in a higher-dimensional space.

This interpretation applies not just to traditional PCA but also to any linear autoencoder that learns matrices W and V with the goal of making the reconstruction of x lie as close to x as possible, Let the encoder be h = f (x) = W (x µ). (13.19) > � 499
